1	package security
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5	
6		"charm.land/bubbles/v2/table"
7		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
8		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
9	
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/scan"
12		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
15		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/shortcut"
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
17		uiviewer "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/viewer"
18	)
19	
20	// findingColumns describes the findings table.
21	//
22	// The table opens on the order the scanner reported — `SortColumn: -1`, which
23	// datatable keeps as a stop on the cycle, so `.` always leads back to it. Every
24	// column sorts, because `.` was handed back to the sort when the severity floor
25	// became four tokens (§3.26) and then no column was ever given a `Less`:
26	// CycleSort returned on its first line and the header advertised a key that did
27	// nothing at all.
28	//
29	// Three columns search, and that is not optional either. Declaring tokens makes
30	// `Searchable()` true, so `/` already opened a query — against no searchable
31	// column, which matches nothing and empties the table. The bar's own left half
32	// says `/ search...` whether or not anything answers it.
33	//
34	// Severity searches nothing on purpose: c/h/m/l are the severity filter, and a
35	// second way to ask one question is what this codebase spends its time
36	// removing. The Title is not pre-truncated either — bubbles cuts every cell to
37	// its column width with the same ellipsis, and doing it by hand at width-3
38	// first only cost three characters of title.
39	func findingColumns() []datatable.Column[scan.Finding] {
40		return []datatable.Column[scan.Finding]{
41			{
42				Title: "Severity", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 10,
43				Cell: func(f scan.Finding) string { return string(f.Severity) },
44				// The same palette the selected row uses, so a severity reads the
45				// same colour whether or not the cursor is on it.
46				Style: func(f scan.Finding) lipgloss.Style { return theme.SeverityTextStyle(string(f.Severity)) },
47				Less:  func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return severityRank(a.Severity) < severityRank(b.Severity) },
48			},
49			{
50				Title: "ID", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 18,
51				Cell:   func(f scan.Finding) string { return f.ID },
52				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return a.ID < b.ID },
53				Search: func(f scan.Finding) string { return f.ID },
54			},
55			{
56				Title: "Title", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 20, Flex: 1,
57				// The Pod Security label is a prefix of the text (DEVDESK-686); the
58				// sort stays on the title and the search sees the label.
59				Cell:   titleWithLabel,
60				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return a.Title < b.Title },
61				Search: func(f scan.Finding) string { return titleWithLabel(f) + " " + f.PkgName + " " + f.File },
62			},
63			{
64				Title: "Source", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 14,
65				Cell:   sourceDisplay,
66				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return sourceDisplay(a) < sourceDisplay(b) },
67				Search: sourceDisplay,
68			},
69			{
70				// Appended last, so the indices above do not move. No Less and no
71				// Search: the Title search already matches the file, and a second
72				// way to ask the same question is noise. It keeps the end of a long
73				// path, which is what tells two findings apart.
74				Title: "File", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 16, MaxWidth: 40,
75				Optional: true, TruncateHead: true,
76				Cell: fileCell,
77			},
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// fileColumn is the index of the File column in findingColumns.
82	const fileColumn = 4
83	
84	// fileCell is the File cell: plain text (Rule 122), with the scanner container's
85	// mount removed and a path under HOME folded. The columns are built once, before
86	// any result exists, so the cell does not know the scanned target (the detail
87	// does): an absolute path under the target shows as the folded absolute path here
88	// and as a relative one in the detail. Trivy reports relative paths, so this is
89	// the rare case.
90	func fileCell(f scan.Finding) string { return shortPaths(f.File, "") }
91	
92	// severityRank orders the levels by how bad they are, which is the only order
93	// worth sorting this column by: alphabetically, CRITICAL lands between no two
94	// levels it belongs with — HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM — so a descending sort would put
95	// MEDIUM at the top and bury the finding the user opened the view for.
96	//
97	// Ascending is least-severe-first, so `.`'s second press (descending, Rule 111)
98	// is the one that answers "what is worst here".
99	//
100	// UNKNOWN ranks below LOW rather than above CRITICAL: it is what a scanner
101	// says when it has no score, not a claim that something is worse than critical.
102	// It has no token either, for the same reason — see severityToken.
103	func severityRank(s scan.SeverityLevel) int {
104		switch s {
105		case scan.SeverityCritical:
106			return 4
107		case scan.SeverityHigh:
108			return 3
109		case scan.SeverityMedium:
110			return 2
111		case scan.SeverityLow:
112			return 1
113		default:
114			return 0
115		}
116	}
117	
118	// findingSelectedStyles colours the selected row by the severity under the
119	// cursor. It is what refreshSelectionStyle did, minus its own bounds check.
120	func findingSelectedStyles(f scan.Finding) table.Styles {
121		return theme.TableStylesForSeverity(string(f.Severity))
122	}
123	
124	// Tab constants for results view
125	const (
126		TabCVE       = 0
127		TabSecrets   = 1
128		TabLicense   = 2
129		TabMisconfig = 3
130		TabCIScore   = 4
131		// TabRemediation is not a category of finding: it has no entry in
132		// tabCategory and its body is its own table (remediation.go).
133		TabRemediation = 5
134		tabCount       = 6
135	)
136	
137	// updateFindingsTable populates the findings table based on active tab and filters.
138	//
139	// The tab is this view's own filter, not the component's: it selects which
140	// findings exist at all, where a FilterBar query narrows a list that is already
141	// settled. The severity went the other way — it is four cumulative tokens the
142	// table owns (Rule 136), which is what gave `.` back to the sort.
143	func (m *Model) updateFindingsTable() {
144		if m.result == nil {
145			return
146		}
147	
148		m.findingsTable.SetItems(m.filterFindingsByTab())
149		// A change of tab or severity is a change of scope, not a shorter list, so
150		// the cursor goes back to the top and the columns are measured again.
151		// SetItems deliberately does neither on its own.
152		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
153		m.findingsTable.Remeasure()
154	}
155	
156	// tabCategory maps a tab to the finding category it shows.
157	//
158	// The tabs and scan.Result's counters are now the same classification, applied
159	// once in scan.Categorize: they were two rules that disagreed on three inputs,
160	// each of which produced a finding counted in the header but present in no tab
161	// at all — visible nowhere, which is the worst way for a finding to be wrong.
162	var tabCategory = map[int]scan.Category{
163		TabCVE:       scan.CategoryVulnerability,
164		TabSecrets:   scan.CategorySecret,
165		TabLicense:   scan.CategoryLicense,
166		TabMisconfig: scan.CategoryMisconfiguration,
167		TabCIScore:   scan.CategoryCIScore,
168	}
169	
170	// filterFindingsByTab returns findings filtered by the active tab
171	func (m *Model) filterFindingsByTab() []scan.Finding {
172		if m.result == nil {
173			return nil
174		}
175	
176		want, ok := tabCategory[m.activeTab]
177		if !ok {
178			return nil
179		}
180		var filtered []scan.Finding
181		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
182			if scan.Categorize(f) == want {
183				filtered = append(filtered, f)
184			}
185		}
186		return filtered
187	}
188	
189	// sourceDisplay returns a display string for the source column.
190	//
191	// Which tool found it, not which category it is — the tab already says the
192	// category, and telling gitleaks from trivy-secret in the Secrets tab is the
193	// point of showing both there.
194	//
195	// A Trivy misconfiguration shows its dialect instead (§3.80): "misconfig"
196	// only repeated the tab's name, while "kubernetes", "helm" or "dockerfile"
197	// is what tells a Deployment's rule from a Dockerfile's on a tab that lists
198	// both — and it is searchable, so `/helm` narrows to the charts. A column of
199	// its own was the alternative, but every other tab would have carried it
200	// empty. A result cached before the dialect was recorded keeps "misconfig".
201	func sourceDisplay(f scan.Finding) string {
202		switch f.Source {
203		case scan.SourceTrivyLicense:
204			return "license"
205		case scan.SourceTrivyMisconfig:
206			if f.IaCType != "" {
207				return f.IaCType
208			}
209			return "misconfig"
210		case scan.SourceKubeconform:
211			// Schema validation, which is what separates it from Trivy's
212			// kubernetes findings on the same manifest.
213			return "schema"
214		case scan.SourceHelm:
215			// Not "helm": that is already the dialect of Trivy's chart findings.
216			return "helm lint"
217		case scan.SourceKustomize:
218			return "kustomize"
219		case scan.SourceBuildContext:
220			// DevDesk's own check (§3.81): what a COPY of the whole context takes
221			// into the image, which no scanner reports.
222			return "context"
223		case scan.SourceGitleaks:
224			return "gitleaks"
225		case scan.SourceTrivySecret:
226			return "trivy"
227		case scan.SourceTrivy:
228			return "vuln"
229		default:
230			return f.Source
231		}
232	}
233	
234	// countFindingsByTab returns the count of findings for each tab. These are the
235	// numbers on the tab labels, and scan.Result's counters are the same ones.
236	func (m *Model) countFindingsByTab() (cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci int) {
237		if m.result == nil {
238			return 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
239		}
240	
241		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
242			switch scan.Categorize(f) {
243			case scan.CategoryVulnerability:
244				cve++
245			case scan.CategorySecret:
246				secrets++
247			case scan.CategoryLicense:
248				licenses++
249			case scan.CategoryMisconfiguration:
250				misconfigs++
251			case scan.CategoryCIScore:
252				ci++
253			}
254		}
255		return cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci
256	}
257	
258	// enterTab is what entering a tab starts: the Dockerfile read of the
259	// Remediation tab, the invalid-setting warning of the Misconfigurations one.
260	func (m *Model) enterTab() tea.Cmd {
261		return tea.Batch(m.enterRemediationTab(), m.enterPSSTab())
262	}
263	
264	// enterRemediationTab reads the Dockerfiles when the tab just switched to is the
265	// Remediation one, and does nothing on any other.
266	func (m *Model) enterRemediationTab() tea.Cmd {
267		if m.activeTab != TabRemediation {
268			return nil
269		}
270		return m.enterRemediation()
271	}
272	
273	// switchTab switches to the given tab index and refreshes the table
274	func (m *Model) switchTab(tab int) {
275		m.activeTab = tab
276		// The Pod Security filter belongs to one visit of the Misconfigurations
277		// tab: it is off on the way in and on the way out.
278		// Only when it is on: switching off an off token rebuilds the rows and
279		// measures the columns again for nothing.
280		if m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(pssToken) {
281			m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(pssToken, false)
282		}
283		// The CI tab carries a score line above the table, so the height changes
284		// with the tab and not only with the window.
285		m.resizeFindings()
286		m.footer.Clear()
287		m.updateFindingsTable()
288	}
289	
290	// handleIgnoreSecret prompts confirmation to ignore a secret finding.
291	//
292	// Gitleaks findings only. .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint,
293	// which a Trivy secret does not have — AddToGitleaksIgnore would fabricate one
294	// from the file and rule, write it, and report success for a line Gitleaks will
295	// never match and Trivy never reads. Refusing says so instead.
296	func (m Model) handleIgnoreSecret() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
297		if exclude := m.canExclude(); !exclude.Enabled() {
298			return m, m.footer.Warn(exclude.Reason)
299		}
300		finding, _ := m.findingsTable.Selected()
301		m.findingToIgnore = &finding
302		m.confirmModal = sharedcomponents.NewConfirmModal(
303			"Ignore Secret",
304			fmt.Sprintf("Add this secret to .gitleaksignore?\n\nFile: %s\nRule: %s", finding.File, finding.ID),
305		)
306		return m, nil
307	}
308	
309	// The two findings actions, and why each does not apply (Rule 130).
310	const (
311		reasonNoFinding    = "No finding selected"
312		reasonNotASecret   = "REDACTED"
313		reasonNotGitleaks  = "Only Gitleaks findings can be added to .gitleaksignore"
314		reasonNotCITab     = "The resolved pipeline belongs to the CI tab"
315		reasonNotARepo     = "An image has no pipeline"
316		reasonNoResolution = "This forge does not resolve a pipeline server-side"
317		reasonNothingToSee = "No finding to open"
318	)
319	
320	// canOpenFinding reports whether enter has a row to detail.
321	func (m Model) canOpenFinding() shortcut.Availability {
322		if _, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); !ok {
323			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNothingToSee)
324		}
325		return shortcut.Availability{}
326	}
327	
328	// canExclude reports whether X applies to the selected finding.
329	//
330	// .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint, which a Trivy secret
331	// does not have — fabricating one would report success for a line nothing will
332	// ever match. The tab is checked first because it is the coarser answer: on
333	// the CVE tab the key means nothing at all, whatever the row.
334	// openPipelineKey opens the pipeline the forge resolves for this repository.
335	//
336	// It is a **declared exception** to the uppercase vocabulary
337	// (keymap.DeclaredExceptions), on the precedent of `c` in oci/network-inspect
338	// and for the reason written there: the action exists on one sub-screen, and
339	// burning one of the three remaining free capitals for it would cost more than
340	// it returns.
341	//
342	// `o` and not `p`: `o` already means "open what this screen points at" in this
343	// view's details state, where it opens a finding's reference. One verb, two
344	// screens, and the shortcut column is replaced by the mode either way.
345	const openPipelineKey = "o"
346	
347	// canOpenPipeline decides whether the resolved pipeline can be fetched.
348	//
349	// The tab is checked first for canExclude's reason — it is the coarser answer,
350	// and off the CI tab the key means nothing whatever the row. The shape is
351	// checked before anything is read: a GitHub context cannot answer this at all,
352	// and finding that out after a keystroke and a git call would be worse than
353	// saying so in the column.
354	func (m Model) canOpenPipeline() shortcut.Availability {
355		switch {
356		case m.activeTab != TabCIScore:
357			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotCITab)
358		case m.result == nil || m.result.TargetType != scan.TargetDirectory:
359			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotARepo)
360		case !forge.ShapeFor(m.config.Forge.Type).MergedCIConfig:
361			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoResolution)
362		}
363		return shortcut.Availability{}
364	}
365	
366	// openResolvedPipeline hands the document to the router, which opens the
367	// viewer on it. The fetch is the source's, so it runs on the viewer's own Cmd
368	// (Rule 110) and its failures are reported where the document would have been.
369	func (m Model) openResolvedPipeline() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
370		// The refusal is never silent (Rule 130), and it is a Warn rather than an
371		// Error: nothing failed, the key does not apply as asked (Rule 128). The
372		// reason is the one canOpenPipeline computed, so the footer and the greyed
373		// entry cannot be about different things.
374		if a := m.canOpenPipeline(); !a.Enabled() {
375			return m, m.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
376		}
377		source := pipelineSource{
378			RepoPath: m.result.Target,
379			Label:    theme.FoldHome(m.result.Target),
380			Forge:    m.config.Forge,
381			Secrets:  m.secrets,
382			Findings: m.result.Findings,
383		}
384		return m, func() tea.Msg { return uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: source} }
385	}
386	
387	func (m Model) canExclude() shortcut.Availability {
388		if m.activeTab != TabSecrets {
389			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotASecret)
390		}
391		finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected()
392		switch {
393		case !ok:
394			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoFinding)
395		case finding.Source != scan.SourceGitleaks:
396			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotGitleaks)
397		}
398		return shortcut.Availability{}
399	}
400	
401	// handleResultsState processes input in results state.
402	//
403	// The search answers first, and every key below is unreachable while it has the
404	// keyboard: "c" is a character in a query, "esc" cancels the search rather than
405	// leaving the results, and "enter" confirms it rather than opening a finding.
406	// The inventory has had this guard since it gained a bar; this state gained one
407	// the day the severity floor became tokens, and never got the guard with it.
408	func (m Model) handleResultsState(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
409		if m.findingsTable.InEditMode() {
410			return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
411		}
412		if m.activeTab == TabRemediation {
413			if next, cmd, handled := m.handleRemediationKey(msg); handled {
414				return next, cmd
415			}
416		}
417		switch msg.String() {
418		case "esc":
419			// No origin view means this view was opened directly, so esc stays
420			// inside it and goes back to whichever landing state it opened on.
421			if m.OriginView == "" {
422				return m.goHome()
423			}
424			return m, func() tea.Msg { return BackToOriginMsg{Origin: m.OriginView} }
425		case "enter":
426			if finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); ok {
427				// The details view is about a finding, not about a row index — an
428				// index would name a different one the moment the list changed
429				// under it, which is how workspaces got D24.
430				m.selectedFinding = &finding
431				m.state = StateDetails
432				m.sizeDetails()
433				m.detailsViewport.SetContent(m.buildDetailsContent())
434				m.detailsViewport.GotoTop()
435			}
436			return m, nil
437		case "ctrl+r":
438			m.activeTab = TabCVE
439			return m.goHome()
440		case "tab":
441			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + 1) % tabCount)
442			cmd := m.enterTab()
443			return m, cmd
444		case "shift+tab":
445			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + tabCount - 1) % tabCount)
446			cmd := m.enterTab()
447			return m, cmd
448		// 1-4 jumped straight to a tab. They were the application's only numeric
449		// bindings, and an exception in a single view is precisely what §3.26
450		// dismantles — tab reaches all four.
451		case "c", "h", "m", "l":
452			return m.toggleSeverity(msg.String())
453		case pssFilterKey:
454			return m.togglePSS()
455		case keymap.Exclude:
456			return m.handleIgnoreSecret()
457		case openPipelineKey:
458			return m.openResolvedPipeline()
459		case keymap.Scan:
460			// Off the Remediation tab this refuses, with the reason (Rule 130).
461			return m.scanCandidates()
462		case writeRemediationKey:
463			// One key, one verb — write the file — applied to whichever tab's
464			// object. The Remediation tab writes a base image, the
465			// Misconfigurations tab a built-in fix; anywhere else the refusal says
466			// which tab it belongs to (Rule 130).
467			if m.activeTab == TabMisconfig {
468				return m.prepareMisconfigFix()
469			}
470			return m.prepareRemediationWrite()
471		}
472		// `.` is the sort again, and the search and the severity tokens are the
473		// table's (Rule 136).
474		return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
475	}
476	
477	// toggleSeverity flips one severity token. Cumulative: c and h together ask for
478	// "CRITICAL or HIGH", which is the question a threshold cycle could not put.
479	func (m Model) toggleSeverity(key string) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
480		label := map[string]string{"c": "critical", "h": "high", "m": "medium", "l": "low"}[key]
481		m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(label, !m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(label))
482		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
483		return m, nil
484	}
485	
486	// resizeFindings lays the findings table out. Every tab gets the whole height:
487	// the CI tab used to give two rows to a score line above the table, and losing
488	// two findings on one tab out of five — for a letter the inventory already
489	// carries per target — was not worth the jump on every tab switch.
490	func (m *Model) resizeFindings() {
491		// The File column belongs to the Misconfigurations tab: the same rule
492		// there can fire in many files, and nowhere else it says nothing more than
493		// the title. Done here, with the size, so a tab switch and a resize cannot
494		// disagree.
495		m.findingsTable.SetColumnHidden(fileColumn, m.activeTab != TabMisconfig)
496		m.findingsTable.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
497		m.remediation.table.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
498	}

1	package security
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5	
6		"charm.land/bubbles/v2/table"
7		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
8		"charm.land/lipgloss/v2"
9	
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/forge"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/scan"
12		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
15		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/shortcut"
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
17		uiviewer "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/viewer"
18	)
19	
20	// findingColumns describes the findings table.
21	//
22	// The table opens on the order the scanner reported — `SortColumn: -1`, which
23	// datatable keeps as a stop on the cycle, so `.` always leads back to it. Every
24	// column sorts, because `.` was handed back to the sort when the severity floor
25	// became four tokens (§3.26) and then no column was ever given a `Less`:
26	// CycleSort returned on its first line and the header advertised a key that did
27	// nothing at all.
28	//
29	// Three columns search, and that is not optional either. Declaring tokens makes
30	// `Searchable()` true, so `/` already opened a query — against no searchable
31	// column, which matches nothing and empties the table. The bar's own left half
32	// says `/ search...` whether or not anything answers it.
33	//
34	// Severity searches nothing on purpose: c/h/m/l are the severity filter, and a
35	// second way to ask one question is what this codebase spends its time
36	// removing. The Title is not pre-truncated either — bubbles cuts every cell to
37	// its column width with the same ellipsis, and doing it by hand at width-3
38	// first only cost three characters of title.
39	func findingColumns() []datatable.Column[scan.Finding] {
40		return []datatable.Column[scan.Finding]{
41			{
42				Title: "Severity", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 10,
43				Cell: func(f scan.Finding) string { return string(f.Severity) },
44				// The same palette the selected row uses, so a severity reads the
45				// same colour whether or not the cursor is on it.
46				Style: func(f scan.Finding) lipgloss.Style { return theme.SeverityTextStyle(string(f.Severity)) },
47				Less:  func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return severityRank(a.Severity) < severityRank(b.Severity) },
48			},
49			{
50				Title: "ID", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 18,
51				Cell:   func(f scan.Finding) string { return f.ID },
52				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return a.ID < b.ID },
53				Search: func(f scan.Finding) string { return f.ID },
54			},
55			{
56				Title: "Title", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 20, Flex: 1,
57				// The Pod Security label is a prefix of the text (DEVDESK-686); the
58				// sort stays on the title and the search sees the label.
59				Cell:   titleWithLabel,
60				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return a.Title < b.Title },
61				Search: func(f scan.Finding) string { return titleWithLabel(f) + " " + f.PkgName + " " + f.File },
62			},
63			{
64				Title: "Source", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 14,
65				Cell:   sourceDisplay,
66				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return sourceDisplay(a) < sourceDisplay(b) },
67				Search: sourceDisplay,
68			},
69			{
70				// Appended last, so the indices above do not move. No Less and no
71				// Search: the Title search already matches the file, and a second
72				// way to ask the same question is noise. It keeps the end of a long
73				// path, which is what tells two findings apart.
74				Title: "File", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 16, MaxWidth: 40,
75				Optional: true, TruncateHead: true,
76				Cell: fileCell,
77			},
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// fileColumn is the index of the File column in findingColumns.
82	const fileColumn = 4
83	
84	// fileCell is the File cell: plain text (Rule 122), with the scanner container's
85	// mount removed and a path under HOME folded. The columns are built once, before
86	// any result exists, so the cell does not know the scanned target (the detail
87	// does): an absolute path under the target shows as the folded absolute path here
88	// and as a relative one in the detail. Trivy reports relative paths, so this is
89	// the rare case.
90	func fileCell(f scan.Finding) string { return shortPaths(f.File, "") }
91	
92	// severityRank orders the levels by how bad they are, which is the only order
93	// worth sorting this column by: alphabetically, CRITICAL lands between no two
94	// levels it belongs with — HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM — so a descending sort would put
95	// MEDIUM at the top and bury the finding the user opened the view for.
96	//
97	// Ascending is least-severe-first, so `.`'s second press (descending, Rule 111)
98	// is the one that answers "what is worst here".
99	//
100	// UNKNOWN ranks below LOW rather than above CRITICAL: it is what a scanner
101	// says when it has no score, not a claim that something is worse than critical.
102	// It has no token either, for the same reason — see severityToken.
103	func severityRank(s scan.SeverityLevel) int {
104		switch s {
105		case scan.SeverityCritical:
106			return 4
107		case scan.SeverityHigh:
108			return 3
109		case scan.SeverityMedium:
110			return 2
111		case scan.SeverityLow:
112			return 1
113		default:
114			return 0
115		}
116	}
117	
118	// findingSelectedStyles colours the selected row by the severity under the
119	// cursor. It is what refreshSelectionStyle did, minus its own bounds check.
120	func findingSelectedStyles(f scan.Finding) table.Styles {
121		return theme.TableStylesForSeverity(string(f.Severity))
122	}
123	
124	// Tab constants for results view
125	const (
126		TabCVE       = 0
127		TabSecrets   = 1
128		TabLicense   = 2
129		TabMisconfig = 3
130		TabCIScore   = 4
131		// TabRemediation is not a category of finding: it has no entry in
132		// tabCategory and its body is its own table (remediation.go).
133		TabRemediation = 5
134		tabCount       = 6
135	)
136	
137	// updateFindingsTable populates the findings table based on active tab and filters.
138	//
139	// The tab is this view's own filter, not the component's: it selects which
140	// findings exist at all, where a FilterBar query narrows a list that is already
141	// settled. The severity went the other way — it is four cumulative tokens the
142	// table owns (Rule 136), which is what gave `.` back to the sort.
143	func (m *Model) updateFindingsTable() {
144		if m.result == nil {
145			return
146		}
147	
148		m.findingsTable.SetItems(m.filterFindingsByTab())
149		// A change of tab or severity is a change of scope, not a shorter list, so
150		// the cursor goes back to the top and the columns are measured again.
151		// SetItems deliberately does neither on its own.
152		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
153		m.findingsTable.Remeasure()
154	}
155	
156	// tabCategory maps a tab to the finding category it shows.
157	//
158	// The tabs and scan.Result's counters are now the same classification, applied
159	// once in scan.Categorize: they were two rules that disagreed on three inputs,
160	// each of which produced a finding counted in the header but present in no tab
161	// at all — visible nowhere, which is the worst way for a finding to be wrong.
162	var tabCategory = map[int]scan.Category{
163		TabCVE:       scan.CategoryVulnerability,
164		TabSecrets:   scan.CategorySecret,
165		TabLicense:   scan.CategoryLicense,
166		TabMisconfig: scan.CategoryMisconfiguration,
167		TabCIScore:   scan.CategoryCIScore,
168	}
169	
170	// filterFindingsByTab returns findings filtered by the active tab
171	func (m *Model) filterFindingsByTab() []scan.Finding {
172		if m.result == nil {
173			return nil
174		}
175	
176		want, ok := tabCategory[m.activeTab]
177		if !ok {
178			return nil
179		}
180		var filtered []scan.Finding
181		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
182			if scan.Categorize(f) == want {
183				filtered = append(filtered, f)
184			}
185		}
186		return filtered
187	}
188	
189	// sourceDisplay returns a display string for the source column.
190	//
191	// Which tool found it, not which category it is — the tab already says the
192	// category, and telling gitleaks from trivy-secret in the Secrets tab is the
193	// point of showing both there.
194	//
195	// A Trivy misconfiguration shows its dialect instead (§3.80): "misconfig"
196	// only repeated the tab's name, while "kubernetes", "helm" or "dockerfile"
197	// is what tells a Deployment's rule from a Dockerfile's on a tab that lists
198	// both — and it is searchable, so `/helm` narrows to the charts. A column of
199	// its own was the alternative, but every other tab would have carried it
200	// empty. A result cached before the dialect was recorded keeps "misconfig".
201	func sourceDisplay(f scan.Finding) string {
202		switch f.Source {
203		case scan.SourceTrivyLicense:
204			return "license"
205		case scan.SourceTrivyMisconfig:
206			if f.IaCType != "" {
207				return f.IaCType
208			}
209			return "misconfig"
210		case scan.SourceKubeconform:
211			// Schema validation, which is what separates it from Trivy's
212			// kubernetes findings on the same manifest.
213			return "schema"
214		case scan.SourceHelm:
215			// Not "helm": that is already the dialect of Trivy's chart findings.
216			return "helm lint"
217		case scan.SourceKustomize:
218			return "kustomize"
219		case scan.SourceBuildContext:
220			// DevDesk's own check (§3.81): what a COPY of the whole context takes
221			// into the image, which no scanner reports.
222			return "context"
223		case scan.SourceGitleaks:
224			return "gitleaks"
225		case scan.SourceTrivySecret:
226			return "trivy"
227		case scan.SourceTrivy:
228			return "vuln"
229		default:
230			return f.Source
231		}
232	}
233	
234	// countFindingsByTab returns the count of findings for each tab. These are the
235	// numbers on the tab labels, and scan.Result's counters are the same ones.
236	func (m *Model) countFindingsByTab() (cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci int) {
237		if m.result == nil {
238			return 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
239		}
240	
241		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
242			switch scan.Categorize(f) {
243			case scan.CategoryVulnerability:
244				cve++
245			case scan.CategorySecret:
246				secrets++
247			case scan.CategoryLicense:
248				licenses++
249			case scan.CategoryMisconfiguration:
250				misconfigs++
251			case scan.CategoryCIScore:
252				ci++
253			}
254		}
255		return cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci
256	}
257	
258	// enterTab is what entering a tab starts: the Dockerfile read of the
259	// Remediation tab, the invalid-setting warning of the Misconfigurations one.
260	func (m *Model) enterTab() tea.Cmd {
261		return tea.Batch(m.enterRemediationTab(), m.enterPSSTab())
262	}
263	
264	// enterRemediationTab reads the Dockerfiles when the tab just switched to is the
265	// Remediation one, and does nothing on any other.
266	func (m *Model) enterRemediationTab() tea.Cmd {
267		if m.activeTab != TabRemediation {
268			return nil
269		}
270		return m.enterRemediation()
271	}
272	
273	// switchTab switches to the given tab index and refreshes the table
274	func (m *Model) switchTab(tab int) {
275		m.activeTab = tab
276		// The Pod Security filter belongs to one visit of the Misconfigurations
277		// tab: it is off on the way in and on the way out.
278		// Only when it is on: switching off an off token rebuilds the rows and
279		// measures the columns again for nothing.
280		if m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(pssToken) {
281			m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(pssToken, false)
282		}
283		// The CI tab carries a score line above the table, so the height changes
284		// with the tab and not only with the window.
285		m.resizeFindings()
286		m.footer.Clear()
287		m.updateFindingsTable()
288	}
289	
290	// handleIgnoreSecret prompts confirmation to ignore a secret finding.
291	//
292	// Gitleaks findings only. .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint,
293	// which a Trivy secret does not have — AddToGitleaksIgnore would fabricate one
294	// from the file and rule, write it, and report success for a line Gitleaks will
295	// never match and Trivy never reads. Refusing says so instead.
296	func (m Model) handleIgnoreSecret() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
297		if exclude := m.canExclude(); !exclude.Enabled() {
298			return m, m.footer.Warn(exclude.Reason)
299		}
300		finding, _ := m.findingsTable.Selected()
301		m.findingToIgnore = &finding
302		m.confirmModal = sharedcomponents.NewConfirmModal(
303			"Ignore Secret",
304			fmt.Sprintf("Add this secret to .gitleaksignore?\n\nFile: %s\nRule: %s", finding.File, finding.ID),
305		)
306		return m, nil
307	}
308	
309	// The two findings actions, and why each does not apply (Rule 130).
310	const (
311		reasonNoFinding    = "No finding selected"
312		reasonNotASecret   = "REDACTED"
313		reasonNotGitleaks  = "Only Gitleaks findings can be added to .gitleaksignore"
314		reasonNotCITab     = "The resolved pipeline belongs to the CI tab"
315		reasonNotARepo     = "An image has no pipeline"
316		reasonNoResolution = "This forge does not resolve a pipeline server-side"
317		reasonNothingToSee = "No finding to open"
318	)
319	
320	// canOpenFinding reports whether enter has a row to detail.
321	func (m Model) canOpenFinding() shortcut.Availability {
322		if _, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); !ok {
323			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNothingToSee)
324		}
325		return shortcut.Availability{}
326	}
327	
328	// canExclude reports whether X applies to the selected finding.
329	//
330	// .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint, which a Trivy secret
331	// does not have — fabricating one would report success for a line nothing will
332	// ever match. The tab is checked first because it is the coarser answer: on
333	// the CVE tab the key means nothing at all, whatever the row.
334	// openPipelineKey opens the pipeline the forge resolves for this repository.
335	//
336	// It is a **declared exception** to the uppercase vocabulary
337	// (keymap.DeclaredExceptions), on the precedent of `c` in oci/network-inspect
338	// and for the reason written there: the action exists on one sub-screen, and
339	// burning one of the three remaining free capitals for it would cost more than
340	// it returns.
341	//
342	// `o` and not `p`: `o` already means "open what this screen points at" in this
343	// view's details state, where it opens a finding's reference. One verb, two
344	// screens, and the shortcut column is replaced by the mode either way.
345	const openPipelineKey = "o"
346	
347	// canOpenPipeline decides whether the resolved pipeline can be fetched.
348	//
349	// The tab is checked first for canExclude's reason — it is the coarser answer,
350	// and off the CI tab the key means nothing whatever the row. The shape is
351	// checked before anything is read: a GitHub context cannot answer this at all,
352	// and finding that out after a keystroke and a git call would be worse than
353	// saying so in the column.
354	func (m Model) canOpenPipeline() shortcut.Availability {
355		switch {
356		case m.activeTab != TabCIScore:
357			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotCITab)
358		case m.result == nil || m.result.TargetType != scan.TargetDirectory:
359			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotARepo)
360		case !forge.ShapeFor(m.config.Forge.Type).MergedCIConfig:
361			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoResolution)
362		}
363		return shortcut.Availability{}
364	}
365	
366	// openResolvedPipeline hands the document to the router, which opens the
367	// viewer on it. The fetch is the source's, so it runs on the viewer's own Cmd
368	// (Rule 110) and its failures are reported where the document would have been.
369	func (m Model) openResolvedPipeline() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
370		// The refusal is never silent (Rule 130), and it is a Warn rather than an
371		// Error: nothing failed, the key does not apply as asked (Rule 128). The
372		// reason is the one canOpenPipeline computed, so the footer and the greyed
373		// entry cannot be about different things.
374		if a := m.canOpenPipeline(); !a.Enabled() {
375			return m, m.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
376		}
377		source := pipelineSource{
378			RepoPath: m.result.Target,
379			Label:    theme.FoldHome(m.result.Target),
380			Forge:    m.config.Forge,
381			Secrets:  m.secrets,
382			Findings: m.result.Findings,
383		}
384		return m, func() tea.Msg { return uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: source} }
385	}
386	
387	func (m Model) canExclude() shortcut.Availability {
388		if m.activeTab != TabSecrets {
389			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotASecret)
390		}
391		finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected()
392		switch {
393		case !ok:
394			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoFinding)
395		case finding.Source != scan.SourceGitleaks:
396			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotGitleaks)
397		}
398		return shortcut.Availability{}
399	}
400	
401	// handleResultsState processes input in results state.
402	//
403	// The search answers first, and every key below is unreachable while it has the
404	// keyboard: "c" is a character in a query, "esc" cancels the search rather than
405	// leaving the results, and "enter" confirms it rather than opening a finding.
406	// The inventory has had this guard since it gained a bar; this state gained one
407	// the day the severity floor became tokens, and never got the guard with it.
408	func (m Model) handleResultsState(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
409		if m.findingsTable.InEditMode() {
410			return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
411		}
412		if m.activeTab == TabRemediation {
413			if next, cmd, handled := m.handleRemediationKey(msg); handled {
414				return next, cmd
415			}
416		}
417		switch msg.String() {
418		case "esc":
419			// No origin view means this view was opened directly, so esc stays
420			// inside it and goes back to whichever landing state it opened on.
421			if m.OriginView == "" {
422				return m.goHome()
423			}
424			return m, func() tea.Msg { return BackToOriginMsg{Origin: m.OriginView} }
425		case "enter":
426			if finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); ok {
427				// The details view is about a finding, not about a row index — an
428				// index would name a different one the moment the list changed
429				// under it, which is how workspaces got D24.
430				m.selectedFinding = &finding
431				m.state = StateDetails
432				m.sizeDetails()
433				m.detailsViewport.SetContent(m.buildDetailsContent())
434				m.detailsViewport.GotoTop()
435			}
436			return m, nil
437		case "ctrl+r":
438			m.activeTab = TabCVE
439			return m.goHome()
440		case "tab":
441			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + 1) % tabCount)
442			cmd := m.enterTab()
443			return m, cmd
444		case "shift+tab":
445			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + tabCount - 1) % tabCount)
446			cmd := m.enterTab()
447			return m, cmd
448		// 1-4 jumped straight to a tab. They were the application's only numeric
449		// bindings, and an exception in a single view is precisely what §3.26
450		// dismantles — tab reaches all four.
451		case "c", "h", "m", "l":
452			return m.toggleSeverity(msg.String())
453		case pssFilterKey:
454			return m.togglePSS()
455		case keymap.Exclude:
456			return m.handleIgnoreSecret()
457		case openPipelineKey:
458			return m.openResolvedPipeline()
459		case keymap.Scan:
460			// Off the Remediation tab this refuses, with the reason (Rule 130).
461			return m.scanCandidates()
462		case writeRemediationKey:
463			// One key, one verb — write the file — applied to whichever tab's
464			// object. The Remediation tab writes a base image, the
465			// Misconfigurations tab a built-in fix; anywhere else the refusal says
466			// which tab it belongs to (Rule 130).
467			if m.activeTab == TabMisconfig {
468				return m.prepareMisconfigFix()
469			}
470			return m.prepareRemediationWrite()
471		}
472		// `.` is the sort again, and the search and the severity tokens are the
473		// table's (Rule 136).
474		return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
475	}
476	
477	// toggleSeverity flips one severity token. Cumulative: c and h together ask for
478	// "CRITICAL or HIGH", which is the question a threshold cycle could not put.
479	func (m Model) toggleSeverity(key string) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
480		label := map[string]string{"c": "critical", "h": "high", "m": "medium", "l": "low"}[key]
481		m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(label, !m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(label))
482		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
483		return m, nil
484	}
485	
486	// resizeFindings lays the findings table out. Every tab gets the whole height:
487	// the CI tab used to give two rows to a score line above the table, and losing
488	// two findings on one tab out of five — for a letter the inventory already
489	// carries per target — was not worth the jump on every tab switch.
490	func (m *Model) resizeFindings() {
491		// The File column belongs to the Misconfigurations tab: the same rule
492		// there can fire in many files, and nowhere else it says nothing more than
493		// the title. Done here, with the size, so a tab switch and a resize cannot
494		// disagree.
495		m.findingsTable.SetColumnHidden(fileColumn, m.activeTab != TabMisconfig)
496		m.findingsTable.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
497		m.remediation.table.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
498	}

640	`Resolution` is a sentence, not a replacement. What it does is hand the whole
641	thing to a calling agent through `scan_result` and stay the thing that measures
642	the result — see `mcp.md`. A finite catalog of fixes for the recurring Dockerfile
643	rules is phase B of §3.78 and does not exist yet.
644	
645	### The finding detail (DEVDESK-750)
646	
647	`Enter` on a finding opens a scrollable detail (`internal/ui/security/details.go`).
648	It used to overflow the viewport (the text width had a floor of 40 cells, `Match`,
649	`Run:`, `Package` and `Version` had no width at all, and the viewport itself was
650	given the view's width instead of two cells less), print a render failure's whole
651	stderr as a title, and bury the one thing a reader wants, what to do, under the
652	facts.
653	
654	**Layout, measured.** The router hands the details state `H - 12` rows
655	(`shortcut.HeaderRows` 7, one blank row, a two-row footer, the title line and the
656	bottom border) and the viewport frame takes two columns, so the viewport is `W - 2`
657	wide (`sizeDetails`, called from `enter` and from `WindowSizeMsg`, so a resize
658	while the detail is open is right too); `Padding(1)` takes one cell and one row
659	on each side:
660	
661	| Terminal | Viewport rows | Text rows visible (after the top padding) | Text width |
662	|---|---|---|---|
663	| 80x24 | 12 | 11 | 76 |
664	| 120x40 | 28 | 27 | 116 |
665	| 175x50 | 38 | 37 | 171 |
666	
667	**Order.** The header (severity, ID), the title on one line, then the fix status
668	and the remediation, the `Message`, the `Description`, the facts (Source, Type,
669	Pod Security, File, Line, Package, Kind, Version, Fixed In, Match), the `Script`
670	of a CI finding and the `References`. A section is emitted only when it has
671	content, and sections are joined by exactly one blank line (never two). Every
672	value is wrapped at the text width, hanging under its label (`detailsText`,
673	`details_text.go`); a tab and a run of blank lines are normalised first. At 80x24
674	the status is on the fifth text line.
675	
676	**Display only.** `shortPaths(text, target)` removes `<target>/` and the container
677	mount `/scan/` from the title, the Message and the File, folds a path under HOME to
678	`~/`, and ignores a target that is not an absolute path (an image reference). The
679	finding keeps its text, the scan cache is untouched, and
680	`scan.renderFailure` still writes the absolute paths, which is what the cache holds. The title is `oneLine`: the first line, cut with `theme.Ellipsis`. The Message is
681	`cappedLines`: wrapped at `min(width, 110)` cells, 8 lines at most, then `… N more
682	lines` (wrapped lines, not source lines). A Message equal to the title or to the
683	description is not repeated. Widths are measured with `x/ansi`, as the viewport
684	does, never with the `runewidth`-based `theme` helpers.
685	
686	**The fix status.** `fixStatusOf(f, onDisk)` (`details_fix.go`) says it in words,
687	never in a colour or a key name (Rules 130, 134):
688	
689	| Finding | Label |
690	|---|---|
691	| vulnerability with `FixedIn` | `Fix available` (`Fixed in <version>`) |
692	| vulnerability without | `No fix available` |
693	| misconfiguration, catalog rule, directory, no refusal | `Built-in fix available` (the rule's title, and its warning) |
694	| misconfiguration, the rule declines this instance | `No built-in fix for this instance` (the reason) |
695	| misconfiguration on an image | `No built-in fix here` |
696	| misconfiguration with no catalog rule | `No built-in fix` (the missing text, or the generic reason) |
697	| secret, license, CI | no status line |
698	
699	A misconfiguration's status reads `misconfigFixAvailability`, extracted from
700	`canFixMisconfig`, so the shortcut in the header and the detail are one
701	computation (`TestFixStatusAndTheShortcutAgree`).
702	
703	**Command or sentence.** `scan.IsFixInstruction(f)` says whether `FixCommand` is the
704	`Update <pkg> to <version>` sentence written for an ecosystem with no known command
705	(`fixInstruction`, same bytes as before: the cache is unchanged). `fixAction` shows a
706	command as `Run: <cmd>` and a sentence as plain text under Remediation.
707	
708	**The scroll position.** In the details state `status()` returns `Lines a-b of N`
709	(`scrollPosition`) when the content is taller than the viewport, read from the viewport on

709	(`scrollPosition`) when the content is taller than the viewport, read from the viewport on
710	every render: a `Status`, not a footer message, so it does not expire after 3 s
711	(Rule 128), and a warning still wins over it. The footer stays two lines (Rule 124).
712	
713	**The File column.** The Misconfigurations tab has a `File` column
714	(`SizingContent`, 16 to 40 cells, `Optional`, `TruncateHead`, no `Less` and no `Search`:
715	the Title search already matches `f.File`). It is the last column, so it is the first dropped
716	on a narrow terminal, and a long path keeps its end. `resizeFindings` hides it on the other
717	tabs with `SetColumnHidden` (`ui-components.md`). The cell is plain text (Rule 122):
718	`shortPaths(f.File, "")`. The table's columns are built once, before any result
719	exists, so the cell does not know the scanned target (the detail does, through
720	`Model.scanTarget`): it shortens a path under `/scan/`, leaves a relative path as it is
721	(Trivy reports relative paths) and folds any other absolute path under `~`. An absolute
722	`File` under the scanned directory therefore reads `~/repo/k/x.yaml` in the table and
723	`k/x.yaml` in the detail. Giving the cell the target would need the datatable to swap its
724	columns after construction; not worth it for a path Trivy does not emit.
725	
726	**Limits of `shortPaths`.** Only POSIX paths starting with `/` are recognised: a
727	Windows path (`C:\repo\x`) is left as it is. A path containing a space is cut at its first
728	space, so what follows the space is not shortened. `dropBlankLines` (the Message) removes
729	every blank line, so it also drops the paragraph breaks of a Message that is not a stderr.
730	`oneLine` (the ID and the title) and `normalizeText` turn a tab into four spaces and drop
731	carriage returns before measuring: `x/ansi` counts a tab as no cell while lipgloss renders
732	it as four, so a tab-separated title used to span far past the viewport.

# DEVDESK-751 — a structured Fix block in the `:sec` finding detail, and actions from the detail

Story SA, estimated M; this plan measures it at **L** (about 8 production files and 10 test files).
One PR on `feat/sec-detail-fix-block-751`, cut from `07a1e84e` (DEVDESK-750 merged). The architect
wrote this plan in a read-only pass. For each step the tester writes the tests first, then the coder
makes them pass. If the PR grows past what one review can take, split it at step 4: PR-A covers
steps 1-3 (AC1, AC2, display only) and PR-B covers steps 4-8 (AC3-AC7, the actions).

## Blocking questions (asked before step 3 / step 8)

**Q1 — AC7 contrast cannot pass as written. It was measured on 2026-11-23 on the 13 shipped themes
with `theme.ContrastRatio` against `ColorBackground`.**

| Colour | Below 4.5:1 on |
|---|---|
| `ColorDim` (greyed key, shortcut descriptions, `DimStyle`) | 10/13: default/mocha 2.46, frappe 2.23, macchiato 2.38, dark-plus 2.90, nord 1.69, one-dark 2.32, solarized-dark 2.79, tokyo-night 2.76 (passes on latte 5.53, github-dark, github-light, solarized-light 4.99) |
| `ColorSubTitleFg` (today's section headings) | latte 2.81, dark-plus 3.43, solarized-dark 4.08, solarized-light 3.41 |
| `ColorTitleFg` (the ID) | dark-plus 3.63, nord 4.41, solarized-dark 3.43, solarized-light 4.06 |
| `ColorWarn` (`StatusWarningStyle`, the Warning line) | latte 2.64, solarized-light 2.98 |
| `ColorFooterError` | dark-plus 3.24, nord 3.73, one-dark 4.38, solarized-dark 3.49, solarized-light 4.29 |
| `ColorText`, `ColorFooterWarn` | pass on all 13 (lowest: solarized-light Text 5.18, latte/solarized-light FooterWarn 4.51) |

- **A (recommended).** The Fix block uses no `ColorDim`, `SubTitle`, `Title` or `Warn` colour. Its
  labels use a new `theme.DetailLabelStyle` (bold, `ColorText`), all of its text is `ColorText`, and
  the word "Warning:" carries the warning. A test checks that every style of the block reaches 4.5:1
  on every theme. `ColorDim` stays as it is: it marks a greyed key, an inactive component that WCAG
  1.4.3 exempts, and the reason for the greying is shown in the footer as a Warn, at 4.51:1 or more.
  The measurement is frozen in `docs/measurements/2026-11-23-sec-detail-contrast.md` and a separate
  story is opened to retune the palette.
- **B.** Retune `ColorDim`, `sub_title`, `warn` and `footer error` in the 13 themes in this PR. This
  changes the colours of every view and adds about M of effort plus a visual review.
- **C.** The test covers `ColorText` only. AC7 is then met only in part.

**Q2 — The fix-status mapping, a product choice to validate** (default = table below). Two points to
decide: (a) do secrets, licenses and CI findings get a Fix block, with Manual or No guidance
available (the default, as AC1 asks: "1st section")? DEVDESK-750 showed none for them. (b) A
vulnerability with a `FixedIn` becomes `Manual`, since the closed vocabulary has no "Fix available".

Questions with a default (not blocking; the PR mentions each one):
- **Q3.** `O` in the detail: by default it is not bound. `enter` opens the viewer, which already has
  `O` (IDE). This is the brief's hypothesis: 6 keys. Adding `O` would make 7 keys, which still fit
  in the 7 rows at 80 columns.
- **Q4.** `Check` (decision Q3 of the story): `scan.Result` does not record whether the local binary
  or the container ran the scan. By default no Check is shown in 751. Recording the tool would need
  a field in `Result` (a cache change), in a later story.
- **Q5.** A `Run` command wider than the text: by default it is shown on one line cut with `…`,
  and `Y` copies it whole. Real commands (`fixcommand.go`) are under 76 cells unless the module
  path is very long.
- **Q6.** Loading in the footer: by default only the verification re-scan (a job) is announced. The
  fix preparation (a file read plus `git status`, about 50 ms) is not.

## Mapping from the DEVDESK-750 labels to the closed vocabulary (AC1)

`fixStatusOf(f, onDisk)` computes the status at display time. For a misconfiguration the order
follows `misconfigFixAvailability`, so the status and `ctrl+o` stay one computation.

| Finding | 750 label | 751 label | Detail / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| misconfig, target is an image (whether or not the catalog has the rule) | `No built-in fix here` / `No built-in fix` | `Cannot fix here` | `reasonFileNotOnDisk` |
| misconfig, catalog rule, `Declines(f) != ""` | `No built-in fix for this instance` | `Built-in fix unavailable: <reason>` | the Declines reason, after the colon |
| misconfig, catalog rule, directory, not declined | `Built-in fix available` | `Built-in fix available` (unchanged) | Effect = `rule.Title`, Warning = `rule.Warning` |
| misconfig, no catalog rule, guidance present (MissingFor, Resolution or FixCommand) | `No built-in fix` | `Manual` | Do = MissingFor then Resolution |
| misconfig, no catalog rule, no guidance | `No built-in fix` | `No guidance available` | — |
| vulnerability, `FixedIn != ""` | `Fix available` | `Manual` | Effect = `Fixed in <FixedIn>` |
| vulnerability, no `FixedIn` | `No fix available` | `No fix published` | — |
| secret / license / CI (Q2a) | (no line) | `Manual` if guidance, otherwise `No guidance available` | — |

  `m.footer.Warn(a.Reason)`. The case blocks stay under 5 lines (Rule 201).
- Tests:
  - the key set is the same for every fixture (CVE, gitleaks, trivy secret, misconfig built-in,
    image, license, CI, minimal) — `testutil.ShortcutKeys`;
  - for each greyed key, pressing it puts its reason in `RenderFooter` and opens no modal;
  - `X` in the detail of a gitleaks finding opens the same modal as in the results state
    (`confirmModal.View()` is equal byte for byte); the answer is still `SecretIgnoredMsg`;
  - `esc` and `W` are unchanged (existing tests).
- `internal/app` test (`header_test.go` or a new `sec_details_header_test.go`): `renderHeaderContent(nil,
  detailsShortcuts, 80)`, stripped, contains each `<key> Description` whole; the same at 120 and 175.

### Step 5 — ctrl+o from the detail, and the detail rebuilt after the re-scan (AC3) — depends on 4
Files: `model.go` (`setResult`), `misconfig_write.go` (`handleMisconfigVerified`), `view.go`
(`status`), `details.go`.
```go
// refreshDetails rebuilds the detail on the result just put on screen: the same
// finding (sameFinding) is shown again, or, when it is gone, the details close
// to the results. Reports whether the detail is still open. Called from setResult.
func (m *Model) refreshDetails() bool
func (m Model) verifyingStatus() (sharedcomponents.Status, bool) // "Re-scanning to confirm the fix…", Activity: true
```
- `status()` in StateDetails: `verifyingStatus` first (when `misconfigVerifying.Target ==
  targetPath`), then the scroll position. `WantsBlink` already follows `status().Activity`.
- Closing the detail has a reason: when `Cleared`, the existing Info (`… cleared in … — confirmed by
  a re-scan`) explains it. When the detail is closed and `!Cleared`, the existing Warn (`still
  reported`) explains it. No new message is added.
- Tests (temp directory and real DS002 file, fixtures from `misconfig_write_test.go`):
  - `ctrl+o` in the detail, then the Cmd runs, then `MisconfigFixPreparedMsg` arrives: its
    `confirmModal.View()` equals the one from the results state on the same row;
  - Yes, then `MisconfigFixWrittenMsg`, then while verifying the footer shows `Re-scanning` with
    Activity;
  - `MisconfigVerifiedMsg{Cleared:true, Result: without the finding}` gives StateResults,
    `selectedFinding == nil`, and the footer contains `cleared`;
  - `{Cleared:false, Result: the finding with Line+1 and a new Description}` keeps StateDetails, and
    the content shows the new Description;
  - a message for another target changes nothing;
  - `mise run test-race` on the package (Rule 110: everything happens in Update).

### Step 6 — enter opens the file, and Y copies the command (AC4, AC5) — depends on 4; parallelizable with 5
Files: `details.go` (or a new `details_actions.go`), `messages.go`, `security_test.go` (TestMain seam).
```go
var writeClipboard = clipboard.WriteAll // seam; TestMain replaces it with a func that fails the test
// FixCommandCopiedMsg reports the clipboard write of the command under Run (Rule 109).
type FixCommandCopiedMsg struct{ Command string; Err error }
func (m Model) openFindingFile() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) // Cmd → uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: viewer.NewFileSource(path)}
func (m Model) copyFixCommand() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)
```
- Success gives Info `Command copied to the clipboard`. Failure is logged (`ERROR [security] copy
  command: %v`) and shows Error `Failed to copy the command — check logs` (Rule 128).
- Tests:
  - `Y` writes exactly `runCommand(f)` to the recorder (no `$`, no newline) and the footer confirms;
  - a write error gives a footer at Error level;
  - an instruction finding greys `Y` and gives the reason;
  - **never run**: a static test (go/ast over the package's non-test `.go` files) finds no
    `exec.Command*` call whose arguments mention `FixCommand` or `runCommand`, and the files of the
    detail do not import `os/exec`;
  - `enter`: the Cmd returns an `OpenRequestMsg` whose `Source.(viewer.FileSource).Path()` is the
    expected path;
  - `internal/app`: from the detail, `enter` opens the viewer, and `esc` returns to `:sec` in
    StateDetails (the viewer sets OriginView).

### Step 7 — keymap: ctrl+o declared on the detail — parallelizable from step 4
`internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go`: a new exception `{Key:"ctrl+o", Surface:"security/details", Why:...}`
("apply the built-in fix of the finding shown; the same write and the same confirmation, defaulting
to No, as the Misconfigurations tab"), and a test in the style of `trace_source_exception_test.go`.
`Y` and `X` are already in the vocabulary (`Copy`, `Exclude`). No conflict in `:sec`: nothing binds
`Y` there, and the local keys are `c h m l p` in the results state only.
Update `.claude/rules/tui-layout.md` (the list of exceptions, l.104-110) and `docs/architecture/app-shell.md` (l.600).

### Step 8 — help, docs, measurement (Rule 114) — last
- `GetHelpContent`: rewrite the "Finding details" section (the layout, the 6 statuses and what each
  one means, Run copied by Y and never run, Output at most 8 lines). Key bindings: `enter` (detail:
  open the file in the viewer; O there opens the IDE), `ctrl+o` (detail), `Y` (detail), `X`
  (detail). Update `help_activity_test.go`.
- `docs/architecture/scanning.md` § "The finding detail": the layout, the mapping table,
  `subjectFinding`, `refreshDetails`, `runCommand`, the `writeClipboard` seam, the 110 cap, and the
  80-column header measurement.
- `docs/measurements/2026-11-23-sec-detail-contrast.md` (Q1-A): the table above, frozen.
- `mise run ci` green.

## Traps
- Rule 110: `refreshDetails`, the footer and `selectedFinding` change only in Update. The copy Cmd
  takes a **copy** of the command, and the viewer Cmd a copy of the path.
- Rule 130: every greyed reason is a named constant read by the header and the handler. No `os.Stat`
  inside `GetShortcuts`. The key set stays identical from one finding to the next.
- Rule 134: no key name in the viewport (`Run:` shows the command, never "press Y").
- Rule 128: success is Info, a refusal Warn, a failure Error. No green in the footer, and Activity
  comes only from the re-scan.
- `setResult` calls `updateFindingsTable`, which runs `GotoTop`. The detail must therefore never go
  back through `findingsTable.Selected()` (hence `subjectFinding`).
- `theme/styles.go` declares each style twice (the var and the rebuild in `ApplyTheme`). A style
  declared only once keeps the default theme's colours.
- The `writeClipboard` seam is global, so the package must not use `t.Parallel` (same as the other
  seams of the package).
- Widths: use `x/ansi` (as in 750), never `theme.TruncateWidth`.

## Risks
- Effort L rather than M: the tests to migrate (`details_test.go`, 12 occurrences of headings) and the
  verification flow are the bulk of it. Split point: after step 3.
- A user who expected 750's `Fix available` for a CVE will now read `Manual` (Q2b).
- `findingFilePath` does not know whether the file exists: a CI finding (its File names an include)
  or a gitleaks finding from the history opens a viewer that says "file not found". This is accepted
  (Rule 130, "Not knowing").
- Irreversible: none (display, local keys, no cache format change, no `Result` field added).

## DEVDESK-751 : plan rédigé, une question bloque l'étape 3 (contraste, AC7)

**Question bloquante Q1 : AC7 ne peut pas passer tel qu'il est écrit.** J'ai mesuré le contraste des 13 thèmes livrés avec `theme.ContrastRatio`, via un overlay de test en scratchpad (aucun fichier écrit dans le dépôt) :
- `ColorDim` est sous 4,5:1 sur 10 thèmes sur 13 (default 2,46, nord 1,69). Il sert aussi aux touches grisées et aux descriptions de raccourcis.
- `ColorSubTitleFg` (les titres de section actuels) est sous le seuil sur 4 thèmes : latte 2,81, dark-plus 3,43, solarized-dark 4,08, solarized-light 3,41.
- `ColorWarn` est sous le seuil sur latte 2,64 et solarized-light 2,98.
- `ColorFooterError` est sous le seuil sur 5 thèmes.
- `ColorText` et `ColorFooterWarn` passent partout.

Trois options :
- **A, que je recommande.** Le bloc Fix n'utilise que `ColorText` (libellés gras via un nouveau `theme.DetailLabelStyle`), et c'est le mot « Warning: » qui porte l'avertissement. Un test vérifie 4,5:1 pour les styles du bloc sur chaque thème. `ColorDim` reste tel quel : la touche grisée est un composant inactif, exempté par WCAG 1.4.3, et sa raison s'affiche dans le pied de page en Warn (4,51 ou plus). La mesure est figée dans `docs/measurements/`, et une story séparée retouche la palette.
- **B.** Retoucher `ColorDim`, les titres, `warn` et l'erreur de pied de page dans les 13 thèmes dans cette PR : toutes les vues changent, environ un M d'effort en plus.
- **C.** Ne tester que `ColorText` : AC7 n'est couvert qu'en partie.

**Q2 : le mapping vers le vocabulaire fermé est un choix produit à valider.** Les deux points qui le bloquent :
- Une CVE avec `FixedIn` devient « Manual », puisque « Fix available » n'existe plus.
- Les secrets, licences et findings CI reçoivent un statut (« Manual » s'il y a une consigne, sinon « No guidance available »). DEVDESK-750 ne leur en donnait aucun.

Le reste du mapping :

| Cas | Libellé 750 | Libellé 751 |
|---|---|---|
| Misconfig sur une image | « No built-in fix here » ou « No built-in fix » | « Cannot fix here » |
| Règle du catalogue qui refuse ce cas (`Declines`) | « No built-in fix for this instance » | « Built-in fix unavailable: <raison> » |
| Règle du catalogue applicable | « Built-in fix available » | inchangé |
| Hors catalogue, avec consigne | « No built-in fix » | « Manual » |
| Hors catalogue, sans consigne | « No built-in fix » | « No guidance available » |
| CVE sans `FixedIn` | « No fix available » | « No fix published » |

Le statut et `ctrl+o` restent un seul calcul (`misconfigFixAvailability`), vérifié par trois invariants testés. Le plan liste les tests, l'aide et la doc à migrer.

**Questions avec un choix par défaut (non bloquantes, signalées dans la PR) :**
- Q3 : pas de touche `O` dans le détail. `enter` ouvre le viewer, qui a déjà `O` pour l'IDE.
- Q4 : pas de Check en 751. `scan.Result` n'enregistre pas si c'est le binaire local ou le conteneur qui a scanné ; il faudrait un champ dans le cache, dans une story ultérieure.
- Q5 : une commande `Run` plus large que le texte est coupée par « … » à l'écran, et `Y` la copie en entier.
- Q6 : seul le re-scan de vérification est annoncé dans le pied de page, pas la préparation du correctif (environ 50 ms).

**Hypothèse des 6 raccourcis à 80 colonnes : elle tient.** La colonne des raccourcis fait 19 cellules, dont 9 pour `<ctrl+o>`, il reste donc 10 cellules par description. Libellés proposés : `esc Back`, `W Open ref`, `enter Open file`, `ctrl+o Apply fix`, `Y Copy cmd`, `X Exclude`. « Copy command » serait coupé en « Copy comma ». `Y` n'entre en conflit avec rien dans `:sec`.

**Défaut trouvé dans le code actuel :** `canFixMisconfig` et `canExclude` lisent la ligne sélectionnée du tableau. Or `setResult` remet le curseur en haut (`GotoTop`), si bien qu'après un re-scan le détail ouvert ne correspondrait plus à cette ligne. Le plan ajoute `subjectFinding()` (le finding affiché dans le détail, la ligne sélectionnée dans les résultats) et `refreshDetails()` dans `setResult` : le détail est reconstruit, ou fermé avec la raison déjà donnée dans le pied de page (`cleared` ou `still reported`).

**Le plan, en 8 étapes TDD :**
1. Vocabulaire fermé (`fixStatusOf`, `Label()`) ; parallélisable avec 2.
2. Fonctions pures : `runCommand`, `fixSteps`, `whereFacts`, `findingFilePath` (sans aucune lecture disque), `sameFinding`.
3. Mise en page du bloc (Fix, Where, Do, Run, Effect, Why, Output, Refs ; largeur ≤ 110) et test de contraste. Dépend de Q1.
4. `subjectFinding`, les 6 raccourcis et les refus avec leur raison, plus un test du header à 80, 120 et 175 colonnes dans `internal/app`.
5. `ctrl+o` depuis le détail ouvre la même modale (comparée octet pour octet), puis reconstruction ou fermeture du détail et statut « Re-scanning » pendant la vérification.
6. `enter` ouvre le fichier dans le viewer ; `Y` copie via un seam `writeClipboard` remplacé dans `TestMain`, avec un test statique (AST) qui garantit que la commande n'est jamais exécutée.
7. Nouvelle exception keymap `ctrl+o` sur la surface `security/details`, avec mise à jour de `.claude/rules/tui-layout.md` et `app-shell.md`.
8. Aide (Rule 114), `scanning.md`, fichier de mesure, `mise run ci` vert.

**Effort : L plutôt que M.** L'essentiel vient de la migration de `details_test.go` et du flux de vérification. Une seule PR est faisable ; si la revue devient trop lourde, on coupe après l'étape 3 : PR-A pour AC1-AC2 (affichage), PR-B pour AC3-AC7 (actions).

**Pièges et risques notés dans le plan :**
- Chaque style est déclaré deux fois dans `theme/styles.go` (la variable et sa reconstruction au changement de thème) ; un style déclaré une seule fois garde les couleurs du thème par défaut.
- Le seam `writeClipboard` est global : pas de `t.Parallel` dans le paquet.
- Rule 130 : aucune lecture disque dans `GetShortcuts`. Un fichier introuvable (l'include d'un finding CI, un secret trouvé dans l'historique) est signalé par le viewer lui-même, ce qui est accepté.
- Aucun point irréversible : pas de changement du format de cache.

Je n'ai pas pu relire la story dans Plane (pas d'outil Plane dans ma session) : le plan repose sur les critères du brief.
